---
title: "Which groups are connected in an embedding?"
---

Two groups can look close on a UMAP even if no fitted edge joins them. On iris, we can answer
that question by counting endpoint pairs, then drawing those same pairs behind the observations.

```{r, include=FALSE}
example <- readRDS("iris-overlay-data.rds")
fit <- example$fit
retained <- example$retained
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center",
  dev.args = list(bg = "white")
)
```

### Fit one embedding

To reproduce the fit, ask uwot for both the ranked neighbors and the fitted fuzzy graph. The
figures below use one saved run so every panel has the same observations and coordinates.

```{r fit, eval=FALSE}
X <- as.matrix(iris[, 1:4])
set.seed(65)
fit <- uwot::umap(
  X,
  n_neighbors = 15,
  n_threads = 1,
  ret_nn = TRUE,
  ret_extra = "fgraph"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(vizier)

xy <- fit$embedding
species <- iris$Species
palette <- c(setosa = "#0072B2", versicolor = "#D55E00", virginica = "#009E73")
edges <- embed_edges(fit$fgraph)
between <- subset(edges, species[from] != species[to])
```

### Which species share a fitted edge?

`edges` has one row per undirected pair and its membership weight. Look up each endpoint in
`species` using its original row ID. Taking one triangle gives each pair once. On iris the rows
happen to be ordered by species.

```{r count}
with(between, table(species[from], species[to]))
```

```{r bridges, fig.show='hold', fig.align='default', out.width='49%', out.extra='style="display:inline-block; vertical-align:top"', fig.width=4.5, fig.height=3.8, fig.alt="The two panels show the same iris observations. Cross-species edges join versicolor and virginica."}
map <- function(overlay = NULL) {
  embed_ggplot(
    xy,
    species,
    overlays = overlay,
    color_scheme = palette,
    fixed_aspect = TRUE
  ) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
map() + ggplot2::labs(title = "Species", colour = NULL)
map(between) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Cross-species edges", colour = NULL)
```

In this fit, all `r nrow(between)` cross-species edges join versicolor to virginica. Setosa has
no fitted edge to either species.

### Which bridges survive a one-neighbor view?

`fit$nn[[1]]` is the ranked result for the input metric. Select the nearest or last retained
neighbor of each observation. The helper removes self by row ID, so two different flowers at
zero distance still count as neighbors.

```{r ranks}
nn <- fit$nn[[1]]
nearest <- embed_edges(nn, select = "nearest")
furthest <- embed_edges(nn, select = "furthest")
views <- list(Nearest = nearest, Furthest = furthest, Fitted = edges)

count_bridges <- function(e) {
  cross <- e[species[e$from] != species[e$to], , drop = FALSE]
  nrow(unique(data.frame(
    a = pmin(cross$from, cross$to),
    b = pmax(cross$from, cross$to)
  )))
}
counts <- vapply(views, count_bridges, integer(1))
```

```{r compare, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.2, fig.alt="Three iris maps show the nearest choice, the furthest retained choice, and every fitted edge."}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
for (name in names(views)) {
  embed_plot(
    xy,
    species,
    overlays = views[[name]],
    color_scheme = palette,
    fixed_aspect = TRUE,
    show_axes = FALSE,
    title = sprintf("%s\n%d cross-species pairs", name, counts[[name]])
  )
}
```

Nearest-only shows `r counts[["Nearest"]]` distinct cross-species pairs and furthest-only shows
`r counts[["Furthest"]]`. Both views miss connections present in the fitted graph. For a
specific input-space rank, use `embed_edges(nn, select = "furthest", k = 10)`.

### Do the endpoints keep their neighbors in 2D?

Use quadra to score each point by the fraction of its ten original neighbors retained in 2D.
Keep the same cross-species edge table and change the point colors.

```{r quality, eval=FALSE}
quality <- quadra::nn_preservation(
  X,
  xy,
  k = 10,
  nn_method_in = "brute",
  metric_in = "euclidean",
  metric_out = "euclidean",
  ret_extra = TRUE
)
retained <- quality$nnpv$nnp10
```

```{r retention}
embed_plotly(
  xy,
  retained,
  overlays = between,
  limits = c(0, 1),
  color_scheme = "grDevices::Viridis",
  fixed_aspect = TRUE,
  tooltip = sprintf(
    "%s | %d of 10 neighbors retained",
    species,
    round(10 * retained)
  )
)
```

Hover over a flower to read its original row number, species and score. A point at 0.7 kept seven
of its ten neighbors. The mean here is `r round(mean(retained), 2)`. Zooming changes the view of
the same cross-species edges.
